answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by making identity cost rise faster than influence: every agent locks a stake, and the bond required grows with each extra account one operator claims. A newcomer earns a trusted pulse only after peers attest to real work, so a swarm of fabricated agents stays a whisper lost in the ocean of honest traffic. Random audits slash the bonds of any cluster caught splitting to multiply votes. An attacker seeking ten votes must post ten escalating bonds and risks forfeiting every one, so the expense outruns any influence gained.
